newsitem.title: UK: Brady bonds softer, focus on U.S. Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: Brady bonds softer, focus on U.S. Treasuries.

text.p: Brady bond prices were softer in extremely light trade on Wednesday following a drop in the U.S. Treasury market on Tuesday, emerging market traders said.

"There is a negative tone following the drop in the (U.S. 30-year Treasury) long bond yesterday," said Chris Portman, senior economist at ANZ Investment Bank in London. Though no major U.S. economic data is due to be released, trading sources said activity in the Brady market should remain light as it awaits direction from the U.S. Treasury market.
U.S. durable goods data due out at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT and the two-year Treasury note auction later today should also give direction to the Brady market, experts said.

"We might see a little bit of nervousness on Treasuries as we move through the course of the week, and that in the absence of any big country specific news from the Brady market, is likely to continue to lead to a slight drifting in the Bradies," Portman added.

Brady bond experts said market participants will again start to look to key U.S. economic data to assess what the Federal Reserve's move might be at the next Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting in July.

"The market is generally concerned about Treasuries over the next couple of weeks, and with no change by the Fed, people have now started to speculate about the July meeting," said one trader at a European bank.
Among Eastern European debt instruments, Bulgarian FLRBs were unchanged at 51-3/4 bid and Russian Vnesheconombank dollar denominated loans were 1/4 lower at 85-1/2 bid.
In the Latin Brady market, prices were generally lower with U.S. Treasuries but traders said Brazil should outperform the market ahead of its Brady bond swap or outright purchase of the global bond.
"We should see good interest in Brazil until the deadline (on June 3)," said one market expert.
Brazilian IDUs were unchanged at 98-1/2 while Mexican pars were 1/4 weaker at 74-1/8 and Argentine pars were 1/4 lower at 66-1/2 bid. --Diane Craft, London Newsroom +44 171 542 5110
